comments.text: Sixty-four map cells read by $4173 in the captured mode. Columns 8,15,24,30,35,41,50,58 translate to type ten with depth limit32 and nonnegative boundary flag. Other cells among these64 resolve to type zero for the bound lookup, with limit24 and negative boundary flag. The map repeats through mask $5E=$3F; this is a world-coordinate strip, not screen pixels or a full collision simulator.

Sixteen translations of a map cell's low nibble. The captured type-four/five/seven/eight/nine/ten/eleven/twelve entries select type ten, while nibble two/three are negative; $4173 uses zero as their fallback depth-table index.

Sixteen inclusive upper column bounds for $4115: 8,15,24,30,35,40,50,255 followed by255. Opening column41 therefore selects region six; opening35 selects region four. These regions select a route entry after the bank is chosen.

Sixteen selectors for exit regions: first eight are three, then eight zeros. Selector at least three uses the shared PRNG high byte masked with $60, selecting bank offsets0,32,64,96. These numbers select an entry bank, not another room by themselves.

Word table parallel to corridor_command_object_pairs (word n answers pair n). A word with high byte $80 or more is code run by the dispatcher (the routine named in each pair's line comment); a smaller high byte means a message: add $8000 and the text record at that address is shown through $674C (default $134A = $934A, Nothing happens.). 76 words; the last two ($8C54, $8C56) are the defaults for the use-wildcard and the final [0,0] pair.
Zero bytes between the handler pointers and the run-length text stream table; no pair maps here.

Overlay entry stub (first of three, at $8C86): JMP $8D6F (a bare RTS). Resident $6B63 jumps to $8C86/$8C89/$8C8C when a run-length text stream ends; this room defines none, so the hook does nothing.

RTS shared by the movement hook stub.

Per-frame room logic. In order: one-time room setup (corridor_room_init); sound selection by animation state (corridor_state_sound); the peach countdown tick if $9072 is non-negative; the camcorder countdown tick if $900C is non-negative. While $8D8A is negative and the other character is within 20 of the player ($0812), Hoggle introduces himself (text $9852, 28-frame message timer) and the flag is cleared. Sets $0337=$14. While the message timer $8D86 runs, Hoggle is held in the talking pose ($034F=1, $033B=0) and the message area is cleared when it expires. Then Hoggle's behaviour by $8D88: 2 leave (walk away from the player), 1 come to the player and ask What do you want?, otherwise stand and pick a facing in $034F from $0349 and $033F.
Bare RTS, target of the three unused text-hook stubs.

A is a direction code (2 or 6, right or left of the player) for Hoggle's walk $033B. If he is already moving in a different direction, $034F is set to 4 and the direction cleared for this frame; otherwise $033B=A.
Counter of CALL HOGGLE requests Hoggle still refuses after being angered: set to 4 by insult or hit and 1 by refusing the cup, decremented by corridor_call_hoggle, cleared when he accepts a gift.
Frames the current Hoggle message stays on screen; set by his handlers (5 to 28), decremented in the frame callback; at zero the message area is cleared ($0836).
Alternates 0 and 1 on each CALL ROCKS: 0 shows the unanswered shout, 1 shows What would you like to call them?.
Hoggle behaviour: 0 idle, 1 coming to the player (set by CALL HOGGLE), 2 leaving after an insult, hit or refused cup, 7 idle after taking a gift. Used by corridor_room_frame_callback.
Negative means the one-time setup in corridor_room_init has still to run; it clears it to zero (the snapshot value).
Negative until the player first gets within 20 of Hoggle; the frame callback then shows his introduction and stores the (nonnegative) distance here.

One-time setup, run while $8D89 is negative: clears it, installs the blocked-command list at $98C1 with $0833 (verb/object entries the room disables), changes the pronoun word byte at $942F to $13 (she) when $052C is nonzero, and sets $0378=5, $0377=$0A.

INSULT HOGGLE. Requires him near ($082D, limit $25). Sets $0564=$FF (he is unfriendly again), $8D85=4, $8D88=2 (leaves), timer 8, sound $25 from the near check, and prints text $95A0 (If that's how you feel, then GOOD BYE.).
HIT HOGGLE. As corridor_insult_hoggle (near check $25, $0564=$FF, $8D85=4, mode 2) but timer 5 and text $935E (Why did you do that?).
GIVE CUP. Requires Hoggle near (limit $20). He refuses with text $9324 (No thank you!), sets $0564=$FF, $8D85=1, mode 2 (leaves) and timer 5. The cup is not consumed.
GIVE with any object not otherwise handled. Requires Hoggle near ($20), timer 5, text $9324 (No thank you!). No state change.
GIVE HELMET. Requires Hoggle near ($20). When $0264 is nonnegative (helmet already worn) it prints $98A7 (It's stuck to your head!); otherwise it continues to the gift-accepted path.

GIVE POPCORN. Requires Hoggle near ($20). When $056D is negative (only the empty box is left) he accepts it: text $92D8 (Cardboard! I've never had cardboard before! Thanks!) through corridor_hoggle_gift_consume, timer $16. Otherwise text $9311 (I'm not hungry.), timer 8.
GIVE for bracelet, camcorder, crystal ball, dollar bill, key, nickel, perfume, quarter and ticket. Requires Hoggle near ($20), then falls into corridor_hoggle_takes_gift.
Hoggle accepts a gift: text $92C5 (Why, thank you!), then corridor_hoggle_gift_consume.
Prints the message at X:Y ($0827), removes the selected inventory unit ($080F), sets $0564=0 (Hoggle befriended), $8D85=0, mode 7, timer 8, and increments the gift counter $8F16.
EAT TICKET. Consumes the ticket ($080F) and prints $9100 (You force yourself to eat it, it tastes surprisingly good.).
EAT POPCORN. If $056D is negative the box is empty: text $90DF (All you have is an empty box.). Otherwise sets $056D=$FF and prints $90A4 (the worst popcorn you have ever tasted).

ASK HOGGLE. Requires him near ($25), timer 15. When $0564 is zero (befriended) it prints a hint: $96F4 (Nothing is as it seems here...) while the gift counter $8F16 is zero, otherwise $96B6 (When is a door not a door? ...graffiti). When unfriendly it cycles four replies by $8F15: $9737, $9776, $979F, $9776, then advances $8F15 modulo 4.
Helper: continues only when the player's translated map type $B0 is $0A (a door column). Otherwise drops its caller's return address and prints $9891 (There's no door here.).
ASK, CONGRATULATE or HIT DOOR. Needs a door cell (corridor_require_door_cell), then prints $934A (Nothing happens.).
Rotating index 0 to 3 of the unfriendly ASK HOGGLE replies.
Gifts Hoggle has accepted, minus one; starts at $FF and is incremented by corridor_hoggle_gift_consume. Zero selects the first hint in corridor_ask_hoggle.

CALL HOGGLE. Within distance $25 ($0812): timer 12, text $94B1 (I'm here! You don't have to shout!). Farther away: while $8D85 is nonzero it decrements it and prints $947F (He doesn't want to talk to you.); at zero it sets $8D88=1 (come) and prints $94A2 (I'm coming!).
CALL ROCKS. Toggles $8D87: first $923C (Here, rocks! Here, rocks! They don't seem to answer.), then $9273 (What would you like to call them?), and so on.
CALL ELEPHANT. Flag $0566 clear: $95CF (Elephant? There's no elephant inside the Labyrinth.); set: $9604 (It will not come now.).
CONGRATULATE ELEPHANT. Flag $0566 clear: $95CF; set: $9572 (The elephant would be pleased if it herd you.).
CONGRATULATE HOGGLE. Requires him near ($25), timer 10. Befriended ($0564 zero): $9523 (You really think so? Aw, thanks!); otherwise $94EC (Oh, you want something do you? That won't work!).
ADUMBRATE ELEPHANT. First use sets $0566, queues sound $1A and prints $9182 (Consider the elephant adumbrated.). Later uses print $9199 (The elephant has already been adumbrated.).
ADUMBRATE JARETH. Calls the resident jingle starter $0869 (reset sound streams and play the three-voice sequence at $2679); no text.
ADUMBRATE DOOR. Needs a door cell, then falls into the shared body.
ADUMBRATE WALL (and the shared body of ADUMBRATE DOOR). Alternates through $0567: $91C2 (You must be joking.) then $91D9 (You can't adumbrate that.), toggling the flag each time.
OPEN DOOR. Needs a door cell, then prints $916C (It's already opened.).
OPEN WALL. On a door cell ($B0 is $0A) prints $916C (It's already opened.); elsewhere $934A (Nothing happens.).

TAKE. Queries the player's cell ($0818). When its translated type is negative the cell is replaced with 0 through $0815 (the item on the floor is taken); otherwise prints $913F (There is nothing to take.).
Frame countdown for USE CAMCORDER; $FF when idle, started at $12.
USE CAMCORDER. Clears $057D and $03A8 and starts the countdown $900C at $12.
Per-frame tick of the camcorder countdown. When the old count was $10 it queues sound $1F. Past zero it decrements $03A8 (to $FF) and prints $9826 (Boy, will they be surprised back home!).
Per-frame: queues sound $18 when animation counter $0298 is 3, or sound $19 when $02A8 is 1 (the second wins), otherwise nothing.
USE HELMET. When $0264 is negative it sets $0264=0 (worn) and queues sound 9. Otherwise prints $98A7 (It's stuck to your head!).
Shared tail: A=5, then tail-calls the resident message display $0827 with the text at X:Y (Y low, X high).
TIME. JMP $0848, which prints the remaining hours and minutes.
Frame countdown after eating the peach; $FF when idle, started at $12.
EAT PEACH. Sets $02B7=0, starts the countdown $9072 at $12 and consumes the peach ($080F).

Per-frame tick of the peach countdown: decrements $9072 and calls $084B with the old count in A. At $11 and $0E it queues sounds $2D and $10; at 0 the resident routine removes an hour ($0376) and, in text mode, requests the scene stored at $0346/$0345.
USE PERFUME. JMP $085A, the resident hint routine on $057A.
LOAD GAME. JMP $0875, resident load dialog.
SAVE GAME. JMP $0878, resident save dialog.
